Breaker, Breaker
BRAY-ker, BRAY-ker
phrase (Boomer slang)
Citizens Band radio protocol of the 1960s–70s: a driver wishing to enter a busy channel "breaks" in by saying breaker, usually followed by the channel number ("Breaker one-nine" for channel 19, the truckers’ channel), and waits for the others to yield. Doubled for emphasis, breaker, breaker became one of the signature sounds of the 1975–77 CB craze and of the trucker films and songs it produced.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Breaker, breaker is how a CB user asked to break into a conversation already in progress: a polite interruption, a request for the floor. "Breaker one-nine, this here’s the Rubber Duck." The Christian observation: the phrase is a small lesson in courteous speech, and a large picture of prayer. On the radio, the man who wanted to speak announced himself and waited; the channel was shared, and you did not simply talk over everybody. That is the wisdom of Proverbs: "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him" (Pro 18:13). Our children live in a world of constant interruption, and the old CB courtesy is worth reviving: ask, wait, then speak. But the larger picture is this. Every believer has a channel that is never too busy. "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not" (Jer 33:3). "Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me" (Psa 50:15). God does not merely let us break in; He promises, "before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear" (Isa 65:24). No trucker on a lonely stretch at three in the morning ever had a channel like that.

Webster 1828 Definition

1970s CB-radio call to enter a busy channel ("Breaker one-nine") — a model of courteous speech (Pro 18:13) and a picture of prayer to the God who answers before we call (Isa 65:24).

expand to see more

BREAKER, BREAKER, interj. (CB-radio slang, 1960s–70s; Boomer era) A call requesting permission to break into a channel and speak, usually followed by the channel number: "Breaker one-nine." Breaker (n.), one who breaks in on a channel.

Webster (1828) — BREAKER, noun The person who breaks any thing; a violator or transgressor; as a breaker of the law. 1. A rock which breaks the waves; or the wave itself which breaks the waves; or the wave itself which breaks against a rock, a sand bank, or the shore, exhibiting a white foam. 2. A pier, mound or other solid matter, placed in a river, to break the floating ice, and prevent it from injuring a bridge below; called also ice-breaker.

Decode for families: the CB rule was ask, wait, then speak. A good rule for the dinner table.

Key Scripture

Pro 18:13 — "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him."

Jer 33:3 — "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not."

Psa 50:15 — "And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me."

Modern Corruption

Harmless radio etiquette; its lesson is courtesy, and its picture is prayer to the God whose channel is never busy.

expand to see more

There is little to correct in breaker, breaker itself. The CB code of courtesy — identify yourself, ask for the channel, yield to emergencies — was better than the manners of most modern comment sections. If anything, the phrase rebukes us. A generation that grew up asking for the floor has raised a generation that interrupts by default, in person and online. James’s rule — swift to hear, slow to speak — was easier to keep when the radio forced you to wait your turn.

The word breaker has an older meaning in Scripture: Micah’s "breaker," the One who goes up before His people and breaks open the way. The believer who calls on God does not merely break into a conversation; he is heard by the One who has already broken through every barrier between God and man. Psalm 141:3 is a fitting prayer before any microphone: "Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips."

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English brecan (to break) → breaker → 1960s–70s CB protocol "breaker" / "breaker one-nine" → breaker, breaker.

expand to see more

Old English brecan — to break, to burst, to violate

Breaker — one who breaks; also a wave breaking on rocks (see Breaker)

1958: Citizens Band radio opened to the public by the FCC

1960s–70s: breaker — CB call to enter a channel; channel 19 the truckers’ channel

Scripture: Mic 2:13 — "The breaker is come up before them"

Usage

""Breaker, breaker — can I say something before you two finish arguing?""

"Call unto me, and I will answer thee (Jer 33:3)."

"He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him (Pro 18:13)."
